latest.name: Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM)
latest.category: General-purpose, research, reasoning and multimodal AI
latest.short_verdict: A strong free, source-grounded research workspace: ask questions across PDFs, web pages, YouTube and other material with inline citations, then turn sources into briefs, study aids and audio. Standard access includes 100 notebooks and 50 sources per notebook; AI usage is compute-based and its exact prompt quota is unpublished.
latest.what_it_does: Gemini Notebook (renamed from NotebookLM in July 2026) organizes PDFs, websites, YouTube videos, audio files, Google Docs and Slides into research notebooks. Users can ask questions grounded in selected sources with inline citations, discover and import web sources, and create study guides, briefings, Audio and Video Overviews, mind maps, quizzes, flashcards, infographics and slide decks. The web version offers a fuller feature set than the Android app.
latest.why_try_it: It is especially useful when answers must be tied to a specific set of documents rather than a general chatbot's background knowledge. Put reports, papers, product documents or reference material into one notebook, ask targeted questions, and open citations to inspect the supporting passages. Its source-grounded workflow and multimodal outputs make it distinct from a general multi-model chat service.
latest.free_tier: The Standard tier is free with a personal Google account. Google's plan comparison lists up to 100 notebooks per user and 50 sources per notebook. Standard AI interaction limits are compute-based and vary with prompt complexity, model/features used and chat length; Google does not publish a fixed numeric prompt-per-day allowance. Google says usage limits refresh every 5 hours until the weekly limit is reached.
latest.limits: The exact Standard prompt and generation quota is not published and can change with testing or availability. Notebooks are separate source collections; the free source cap is 50 per notebook. The Android app is an early version: it accepts PDF, website, YouTube, audio and copied text, but does not yet support notes, mind maps, reports, data tables or chat configuration/analytics. Use the web version for the fuller feature set. AI answers and generated media can be inaccurate; citations help verification but are not a guarantee. Consumer-account data is not used to train Gemini Notebook unless feedback is submitted; feedback may expose the interaction context to reviewers.
latest.signup_pakistan: Google's official supported-country list includes Pakistan for browser access, and its Android app rollout list also includes Pakistan. A personal Google Account and sign-in are required; age-of-consent and age-verification rules apply. Work/school accounts may need administrator access enabled. The free Standard tier is available without purchasing an AI plan; local pricing/payment acceptance for paid upgrades was not verified.
latest.quality_evidence: Vendor claim: Google's 16 July 2026 rename announcement reported more than 30 million users and 600,000 organizations; this is Google's own adoption figure. Platform evidence: the official Google Play listing showed 50M+ downloads and 4.7 stars from about 354K reviews when checked on 2026-11-08. Independent evidence: an early-2025 human-judged Benchmarks.law evaluation of 18 real legal-document extraction tasks recorded 14/18 passes (77.8%) for the then-free NotebookLM; this is a small, narrow, older test and not a benchmark of the renamed 2026 release. Anecdotal community feedback: a June 2026 Reddit user described cross-referencing dozens of documents as useful; this is one user's experience, not verified performance evidence. No independent broad benchmark of the current 2026 release was located.
latest.android_status: Official Gemini Notebook Android app by Google LLC is listed on Google Play. Google's support page lists Pakistan among Android rollout countries and requires Android 10 or later. The app is still described as an early version and has fewer source types and features than the web version.
